subject: Fwd: AI Assistant Project
body:
Subject: AI Assistant Project

﻿
________________________________
🎯
Objectif final



Créer un assistant capable de :

  *   Lire du texte (rapport ou mail)
  *   Résumer ce texte automatiquement

________________________________
🗺️
Étapes du programme



Étape 1 : Comprendre les bases de l’IA & du NLP



📚 À apprendre :

  *   Ce qu’est le NLP (Natural Language Processing)
  *   Ce qu’est un modèle pré-entraîné (comme BERT, T5, GPT, etc.)
  *   La différence entre modèle entraîné et modèle à entraîner



🧠 Ressources simples :

  *   Cours IA débutant OpenClassrooms<https://openclassrooms.com/fr/courses/7273881-initiez-vous-a-lintelligence-artificielle>
  *   Video simple sur le NLP (Français)<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RMg87rqPsbE>

________________________________
Étape 2 : Choisir une technologie simple



🔧 Tu as plusieurs choix simples pour intégrer un modèle IA :



✅
Langage recommandé : Python



Car il est le plus utilisé en IA, facile à lire et plein de bibliothèques IA.



Tu peux l’installer avec Anaconda<https://www.anaconda.com/> ou directement Python + VSCode.

________________________________
Étape 3 : Tester un modèle déjà prêt (Pas d’entraînement requis)



Tu vas utiliser un modèle pré-entraîné pour faire des résumés. Exemples :



🧠
Modèle prêt à l’emploi : HuggingFace Transformers



📌 Exemple de modèle de résumé : facebook/bart-large-cnn ou t5-small



💻 Code simple :

from transformers import pipeline



# Charger le pipeline de résumé

summarizer = pipeline("summarization")



# Exemple de texte

texte = """

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company. Our mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

"""



# Résumé

res = summarizer(texte, max_length=50, min_length=20, do_sample=False)

print(res[0]['summary_text'])

✅ Avantages :

  *   Pas besoin de former un modèle
  *   Résultats immédiats
  *   Gratuit jusqu’à une certaine limite (grâce à HuggingFace)



📦 Installe les dépendances :

pip install transformers

pip install torch

________________________________
Étape 4 : Ajouter une interface (facultatif)



Tu peux utiliser une interface web simple :

  *   HTML/CSS pour le design
  *   Python (avec Flask) pour lier le formulaire au modèle IA



💻 Exemple :

pip install flask

Puis tu crées :

  *   app.py (serveur Flask)
  *   templates/index.html (formulaire HTML)



Tu pourras envoyer un texte et voir le résumé.

________________________________
Étape 5 : Lire un rapport ou mail (fichier .txt, .docx ou copier-coller)



Tu peux ajouter une fonction pour lire :

  *   un fichier texte .txt
  *   ou copier-coller dans une zone de texte



Exemple pour lire un .txt :

with open("rapport.txt", "r") as f:

    texte = f.read()

res = summarizer(texte)

________________________________
Étape 6 : Embellir et documenter

  *   Ajouter une interface claire
  *   Résumé dans plusieurs langues ? (possible avec des modèles multilingues)
  *   Documenter ton code pour ton rapport de stage

________________________________
🎁 Bonus : Environnement No-code (si tu ne veux pas coder)



Tu peux utiliser :

  *   HuggingFace Inference API<https://huggingface.co/inference-api>
  *   LangChain + Streamlit<https://docs.streamlit.io/> pour une interface interactive

________________________________
📌 Résumé de ton plan d’action

Étape

Objectif

Outils

1

Comprendre IA et NLP

OpenClassrooms, YouTube

2

Installer Python

VSCode, Anaconda

3

Tester un modèle

HuggingFace, Transformers

4

Créer une interface

Flask, HTML

5

Lire des textes

open(), docx

6

Finaliser et documenter

Rapport de stage

subject: Math-Assignement problem
body:
Here are a set of assignment problems for the Calculus I notes. Please note that these problems do not have any solutions available. These are intended mostly for instructors who might want a set of problems to assign for turning in. Having solutions available (or even just final answers) would defeat the purpose the problems.

If you are looking for some practice problems (with solutions available) please check out the Practice Problems<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/Problems/CalcI/CalcI.aspx>. There you will find a set of problems that should give you quite a bit practice.

Here is a listing of sections for which assignment problems have been written as well as a brief description of the material covered in the notes for that particular section.

Review<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/ReviewIntro.aspx> - In this chapter we give a brief review of selected topics from Algebra and Trig that are vital to surviving a Calculus course. Included are Functions, Trig Functions, Solving Trig Equations and Equations, Exponential/Logarithm Functions and Solving Exponential/Logarithm Equations.
Functions<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/Functions.aspx> – In this section we will cover function notation/evaluation, determining the domain and range of a function and function composition.
Inverse Functions<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/InverseFunctions.aspx> – In this section we will define an inverse function and the notation used for inverse functions. We will also discuss the process for finding an inverse function.
Trig Functions<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/TrigFcns.aspx> – In this section we will give a quick review of trig functions. We will cover the basic notation, relationship between the trig functions, the right triangle definition of the trig functions. We will also cover evaluation of trig functions as well as the unit circle (one of the most important ideas from a trig class!) and how it can be used to evaluate trig functions.
Solving Trig Equations<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/TrigEquations.aspx> – In this section we will discuss how to solve trig equations. The answers to the equations in this section will all be one of the “standard” angles that most students have memorized after a trig class. However, the process used here can be used for any answer regardless of it being one of the standard angles or not.
Solving Trig Equations with Calculators, Part I<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/TrigEquations_CalcI.aspx> – In this section we will discuss solving trig equations when the answer will (generally) require the use of a calculator (i.e. they aren’t one of the standard angles). Note however, the process used here is identical to that for when the answer is one of the standard angles. The only difference is that the answers in here can be a little messy due to the need of a calculator. Included is a brief discussion of inverse trig functions.
Solving Trig Equations with Calculators, Part II<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/TrigEquations_CalcII.aspx> – In this section we will continue our discussion of solving trig equations when a calculator is needed to get the answer. The equations in this section tend to be a little trickier than the "normal" trig equation and are not always covered in a trig class.
Exponential Functions<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/ExpFunctions.aspx> –In this section we will discuss exponential functions. We will cover the basic definition of an exponential function, the natural exponential function, i.e.
e
x
, as well as the properties and graphs of exponential functions
Logarithm Functions<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/LogFcns.aspx> – In this section we will discuss logarithm functions, evaluation of logarithms and their properties. We will discuss many of the basic manipulations of logarithms that commonly occur in Calculus (and higher) classes. Included is a discussion of the natural (
ln
(
x
)
) and common logarithm (
log
(
x
)
) as well as the change of base formula.
Exponential and Logarithm Equations<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/ExpLogEqns.aspx> – In this section we will discuss various methods for solving equations that involve exponential functions or logarithm functions.
Common Graphs<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/CommonGraphs.aspx> – In this section we will do a very quick review of many of the most common functions and their graphs that typically show up in a Calculus class.

Limits<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/LimitsIntro.aspx> - In this chapter we introduce the concept of limits. We will discuss the interpretation/meaning of a limit, how to evaluate limits, the definition and evaluation of one-sided limits, evaluation of infinite limits, evaluation of limits at infinity, continuity and the Intermediate Value Theorem. We will also give a brief introduction to a precise definition of the limit and how to use it to evaluate limits
Tangent Lines and Rates of Change<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/Tangents_Rates.aspx> – In this section we will introduce two problems that we will see time and again in this course : Rate of Change of a function and Tangent Lines to functions. Both of these problems will be used to introduce the concept of limits, although we won't formally give the definition or notation until the next section.
The Limit<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/TheLimit.aspx> – In this section we will introduce the notation of the limit. We will also take a conceptual look at limits and try to get a grasp on just what they are and what they can tell us. We will be estimating the value of limits in this section to help us understand what they tell us. We will actually start computing limits in a couple of sections.
One-Sided Limits<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/OneSidedLimits.aspx> – In this section we will introduce the concept of one-sided limits. We will discuss the differences between one-sided limits and limits as well as how they are related to each other.
Limit Properties<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/LimitsProperties.aspx> – In this section we will discuss the properties of limits that we’ll need to use in computing limits (as opposed to estimating them as we've done to this point). We will also compute a couple of basic limits in this section.
Computing Limits<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/ComputingLimits.aspx> – In this section we will looks at several types of limits that require some work before we can use the limit properties to compute them. We will also look at computing limits of piecewise functions and use of the Squeeze Theorem to compute some limits.
Infinite Limits<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/InfiniteLimits.aspx> – In this section we will look at limits that have a value of infinity or negative infinity. We’ll also take a brief look at vertical asymptotes.
Limits At Infinity, Part I<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/LimitsAtInfinityI.aspx> – In this section we will start looking at limits at infinity, i.e. limits in which the variable gets very large in either the positive or negative sense. We will concentrate on polynomials and rational expressions in this section. We’ll also take a brief look at horizontal asymptotes.
Limits At Infinity, Part II<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/LimitsAtInfinityII.aspx> – In this section we will continue covering limits at infinity. We’ll be looking at exponentials, logarithms and inverse tangents in this section.
Continuity<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/Continuity.aspx> – In this section we will introduce the concept of continuity and how it relates to limits. We will also see the Intermediate Value Theorem in this section and how it can be used to determine if functions have solutions in a given interval.
The Definition of the Limit<https://tutorial.math.lamar.edu/problemsns/calci/DefnOfLimit.aspx> – In this section we will give a precise definition of several of the limits covered in this section. We will work several basic examples illustrating how to use this precise definition to compute a limit. We’ll also give a precise definition of continuity..

AI-powered app building. Made for everyone.

New creative superpowers to turn your vision into an AI-powered app in minutes.

Build apps free of charge<https://c.gle/APy2Ad1uHo3EtkXJrpM9eIbEbfDnY9YhUxpD475RA_hIx7_J_O-20_VtL2df4Kiq6qCL_Xu2lWro2eDHrlnztX4DsA_nbVIQ8JNcY5Q3ZR6ujoRI3WYy-k6jv9kEEtrzJxAeE1KBMuXiIY2Qj0n6pQE_yQlfpxbWJ7GmURIlSzdqo4vgo7aRUoqZRpIYaREIR7Y-SoiDHw1bWElrAOQAkHu0ZXZdUksRJq5NxGcjwTso-A5doLMp>

We’ve been building a better foundation for Google AI Studio. Now, we're making it faster and more intuitive than ever to turn your vision into a working, AI-powered app.

It starts with being a partner that builds alongside you, from the first spark of an idea to the final iteration.

Here’s how we’re bringing this to life in Google AI Studio.<https://c.gle/APy2Ad2mFsJ83mVX710EUMBa3BtbuNWL22UZM_Z6N9NjEXGvPUygcPgNSrB4i1NL11LmLXKAMhYwouuVKP7rYbO4dK32sLjXKFuVAXa5xG9Pn4sxZldMFRuJiNwo2hTF7ePyzB2-kKfFO5dAziHtVjLmjKHkGbBnRtxDCi449JkoFJZ-hxw_oGpjgS5Z33lbY38ztDz_BvkyrE8X9ZweG13rLUpEQkwZ_qi7yg>

A screenshot of the Gemini AI platform interface, showcasing options to build AI applications like image generation, AI chatbots, and conversational voice apps, with the title “Build your ideas with Gemini.<https://c.gle/APy2Ad086Q2CSJjhenqTvW7F2ZfEoUviiAmv5DQAiz-xaZrH4YyOGBRvhb8tfQxxoWThzGZNEqI24TQiC9JYIUxLIPp5y-U9rLNkRrgiQMJ9nhwb1GwVKFVF6xRO2fqfvVfoWEj2ANEHsMEV0Q-nxjeTLdS0zQxY-O_-jY9qvDjoA-qfVFEXP3z7KEKN5BV-l5829rnBhgNcDSZxOYkwW50H4dxmdXLo>

Go from a single prompt to an AI-powered app<https://c.gle/APy2Ad3wwjflApJc8XTU1g7rrAHVS2v0sO8YQz-uWgIZIbU3DldSXruLO0k3U6tRT6qdVHybP-1uZ2jmJutS2YRtYItjZt78WK0NUZkVdjDDtcoXHAnnEqKjjBTZo8sFtNXH5Hx2iVr0N-GjmeiWF6p5futSu3_kehf778OKqzhaajtVQvyNOI7MgdyFBTlHZ0STAv0V7Osqv0-EdlBVf8fWwjuiqBbsS07s2QUAWfhzcUYTIRCGvfugBJAk69gMado>

Traditionally, building an app requires juggling different APIs, SDKs, and services. That complexity can be a major barrier between your idea and a working prototype.

The new vibe coding experience in AI Studio removes that friction entirely, as soon as you start.

Want to make a magic mirror app where you can ask it to take your photo and transform it into something fantastical? Just say so.

A dark-themed user interface displaying a grid of application thumbnails and descriptions, highlighting AI tools for photo editing, video generation, and interactive maps, under the title “Remix and explore the gallery"<https://c.gle/APy2Ad0bThEYcHVEKlirQTXrNlG6bKX82exu7zcPDi3worStICw6pzDGBRB1PPaFi64LvotGqXhX-Go1vc7eWW_Bnnu-KTbvEJnSuJodhq9SXn9dZiupUUagfuKhGND2ylkokN9SKFnKcRIw-2Ej7adMd-I_mj0TbtYbLKn-ZvDwLGn0pcQDm9f6dqzCBBRC_eeHN_6zb8LheXCIZ8-2GODjGnxx4QoJ>

Find inspiration when you need it most<https://c.gle/APy2Ad0J_TrZgwUD35-qu3mMtZrj-YJGuHIMUOm2KLGpNji8sJLGH5_ZRrn_oJHjW3UmOnoC2jUTva-3rQD-qyvGZLhdE80VfL6rqCHiKmRTE95oegai3VtX37e4-SoE-7dLCRl8AhrSp3ayx8SJY17k-uyAdP7m6anubWqsA8KkU7Fhib41mfcs_TteijAN0jm8Sxfw4kA9_quCtLntcQIw9ru2SgnjxdI4IjHMw5YksHlItpUcOw1ArfGXdA>

Sometimes, a spark of inspiration is all you need to get going. To fuel your imagination, we’ve revamped the app gallery into a rich, visual library of what’s possible with Gemini. Explore project ideas, preview them instantly, learn from the starter code, and remix apps into your own creations.

Screenshot of a feature allowing users to remove image backgrounds with AI, showing multiple image layers and a central glowing lightbulb icon, with the text “Add AI-powered background removal.<https://c.gle/APy2Ad1YLgL6Z_MAg_9W6Hxj9eaNO3AKsfpNNk_6drLDAeYzku9zCCtJznDSrXxgPGF1TgnHSV5k4C0XNg9G69IeXAm3PgCJ-fzJKhNyaJhA04L3zvsMhNS4zSs5ahvAl_Q5SAswD68uPQuHBhw_rMlROJBm71p-rk7jeLshnXx35X2VSUzdI0lCbzDQ2mXne1cOXcjDIXMrgguz8SDWTZhic0b84-a3>

And because inspiration can strike at any time, our new loading screen cycles through creative ideas that Gemini comes up with while your app builds, turning wait time into a source of new possibilities.

Screenshot of a feature allowing users to point and edit in Google AI Studio.<https://c.gle/APy2Ad1WCwbZRCk40gyb45oUsGTj3rn1jsfmiL4qOX3IlXKE1VENg0oNyCaCfPR4n_-NxinB6lEQp8BqCSmYu3Yloa9GwLNpTeozqPDVFSreciOCln-zsVIC_w_qwahwVwsR1oNqNbr7GTQqbpZacysUF23MLls1Gq8BGJtd1zExVLPkQuzFiYEzKY1LRDEffWLRpq0Jad7CMWlqAgL1COXwWo_NwzKp>

Make changes to your app in a more natural way<https://c.gle/APy2Ad2gEKILAX9IgixTpERZguKuPhXsgaaeDx_0udAjNR-nJasC_vrZU2zZDE8pu-2x5CkIsfTV2xHCpW4QuAbcx6JWUSC1TzzaJkaF2x-F6CP0PK_s95ScJJqOgcLNYMvfyZlKP94yvxlaQoGEA-LlxNFcTaEinJC_mbCQO42BeKu2VINvVfQPCbCLbwlrGdrFllfsjRyQf6W6JXiT8aEiNNO-98-O4-3YfKenwWTNY5wkimPVEvPoeGLoGZr2JhO1>

Refining your app should be as easy as pointing at what you want to change. Our new Annotation Mode makes this possible. Instead of painstakingly describing a change or digging through code, you can now simply highlight a part of your app and tell Gemini what to modify. Ask it to alter a button’s color, restyle certain cards, animate a selected image, or make any other changes you can imagine.

It’s an intuitive, visual dialogue that keeps you in your creative flow.

These updates are more than just individual features. They’re about giving you new creative superpowers. By integrating AI at every step—from ideation to iteration—we’re making it easier for developers to build amazing apps, and helping those who’ve never written a line of code to bring their ideas to life.

Our goal is to lower the barrier between a great idea and a working app with Gemini, so anyone can build with AI.

Build apps free of charge<https://c.gle/APy2Ad1a1iiZW0TBagxsKOhmtvEO8-PMj_K6VPg4W4WOnN-mStd3anFv3K2YFSliLQIAQEiWAn-YoF_4PEhiKTB5RkxkxFk8lnlBO3gk5HJz39iHIad3RoKiCbvC67ZcRvTqSsCd2F4qnuG63P4mr-FHqg9lfEZ0xWY2hdvfZz_Qbd2k3w3zVwLGlTIXVZL-vXrrR0TLXwZI1suYK1qaDBojGgLrZTsxf_e6Nmp8yKgIo5HbqYM>

Happy vibe coding,
